items.text: The BAS provider chain is text-only (ExecutePrompt(string) → string). Audio capabilities have heterogeneous I/O: Whisper takes audio bytes and returns text, Kokoro takes text and returns audio bytes, Ollama takes text and returns text. The BAS AIProvider interface cannot be reused directly — audio-tools needs per-capability typed interfaces.

The BAS architectural patterns (chain fallback, LPBS credit integration, availability caching, factory pattern, error classification) are highly reusable as design patterns, even though the Go code itself is text-modality-specific. Replicating the pattern per-capability is more practical than extracting a shared generic package.

The LPBS AI gateway currently only supports text-based chat completion endpoints. Routing STT/TTS through LPBS would require new gateway endpoints for audio upload (STT) and audio download (TTS). This is a cross-scenario dependency outside audio-tools scope.

Current web-console audio stack is entirely local-only: Whisper at localhost:8090, Kokoro at localhost:8880, Ollama at localhost:11434. No provider routing, BYOK, or credit metering exists for any audio capability today.

items.context: The BAS text-only interface doesn't fit audio modalities. Three architecture approaches are viable, each with different complexity/flexibility tradeoffs.

options.label: Per-capability typed provider chains
options.rationale: Each capability (STT, TTS, summarize) gets its own Go interface and chain with capability-specific request/response types. Simplest to implement, clearest types, but some boilerplate duplication across chains.

options.label: Generic provider with Go type parameters
options.rationale: One Provider[Req, Resp] generic interface, with concrete types per capability. Less boilerplate but more abstract; Go generics can be awkward for interface-heavy patterns.

options.label: Unified audio gateway with internal routing
options.rationale: Single API surface that accepts all audio requests and routes internally. Cleanest external API but highest internal complexity; may over-abstract early.

items.context: LPBS gateway only supports text chat today. Deciding which audio capabilities should route through LPBS affects credit metering design and cross-scenario dependencies.

options.label: LPBS for summarization only (text-based)
options.rationale: Summarization already fits the LPBS text API. STT/TTS stay local-only or use direct external APIs with BYOK keys. Avoids LPBS gateway changes entirely.

options.label: LPBS for all three capabilities
options.rationale: Full credit metering for all audio operations. Requires new LPBS audio endpoints — significant cross-scenario work but most complete monetization story.

options.label: LPBS for summarization + STT (skip TTS)
options.rationale: STT through LPBS is higher value (cloud Whisper costs more than local). TTS stays local/BYOK only. Moderate LPBS scope.

items.topic: Reuse strategy for BAS provider chain code
items.context: BAS has ~1100 lines of well-structured provider chain code. The question is whether to extract shared infrastructure or replicate the pattern independently in audio-tools.

options.label: Replicate pattern, don't extract shared code
options.rationale: Audio-tools implements its own provider chains following BAS patterns. Avoids coupling, allows audio-specific optimizations. BAS code stays unchanged. Recommended for now since the interfaces differ significantly.

options.label: Extract shared provider-chain package
options.rationale: Extract common fallback logic, availability caching, LPBS reporting into a shared Go package. Both BAS and audio-tools import it. Higher upfront cost but reduces drift over time.

items.text: BAS credit metering uses hard-coded operation costs (security measure — no env var overrides). Audio-tools would need its own operation types (e.g., 'audio.stt_transcribe', 'audio.tts_synthesize', 'audio.summarize') with per-operation cost definitions. LPBS usage reporting uses a standard structure with 'app_bundle_key' and 'LimitKey=ai_credits' that audio-tools can adopt directly.
